unresolved_added: The Summary's `84.6%` is ambiguous; the displayed sample supports negative-class `11/13`, not a general propagation accuracy.
The Summary calls 92.86%/85.22% goodness of fit without giving raw denominators or a conventional fit definition.
The advertised `10.68%` is a negative-class percentage-point increase, not a relative percentage increase or a two-class gain.
Positive-ID fit changes only 0.02 percentage points after update.
The Introduction says the update significantly improves accuracy without a significance test or uncertainty interval.
Limited agency resources are not quantified as staff, hours, travel, budget or service capacity.
The assumption that a nest lies near every confirmed witness report ignores worker travel, transported insects and report-location error.
The paper admits intervention affects the data but does not model removal, traps, publicity or reporting policy.
The no-major-climate-change assumption lacks a time horizon and climatic variables.
Data are declared true and reliable "to a certain degree" without an error model.
Screening to 2019-2020 may discard useful negative-report behavior before the first confirmed sighting.
The 2,127 linked-image count is not reconciled with the later 14 positive and 3,194 negative image counts.
GlobalID/image-name joining has no unmatched, duplicate or many-to-one audit.
PNG, MOV and PDF conversion to JPG omits frame/page selection and quality-loss checks.
Figure 3-1's class counts show extreme imbalance, but later headline metrics still rely on overall or class-aggregate accuracy.
The DEM overlay does not establish that all relevant reports are below 3,000 m or that elevation has no control effect.
The statement that the invader has no natural enemies is not demonstrated for the study area.
Monthly eyewitness-report counts are treated as evidence of colony abundance and reproduction.
Report peaks can reflect publicity, search effort, weather and agency workflow as well as biology.
Equation 4-1 is a linear net-growth recurrence and does not itself express density regulation.
The switch at `N<K/2` versus the later migration trigger at `N>K` leaves the middle regime and threshold logic unclear.
Equation 4-2 combines a logistic density factor with a time logistic denominator without derivation.
Equation 4-3 repeats `Jun-Jul`, overlaps `Oct-Nov` with the zero `Nov-Mar` branch, and leaves month coverage ambiguous.
The seasonal `alpha_i`, mortality `beta`, capacity `K`, correction `r` and migration loss `mu` are not estimated.
The claim that a queen takes about half the colony and moves at most 30 km is not tied to a precise source passage or uncertainty.
Equation 4-4 does not make origin/destination conservation or the role of `mu` clear.
Latitude-longitude increments are not converted through geodesic distance, so the 30 km cap is not operationally specified.
The phrase "spontaneous combustion events" is a domain-inappropriate wording artifact in the Gaussian section.
Gaussian mean and variance are neither defined from data nor estimated.
Equation 4-6 adds density values to coordinates through `p(x)dx` and `p(y)dy` without a sampling or unit derivation.
Independent latitude/longitude Gaussian movement ignores map projection, anisotropy, barriers and spatial covariance.
The source correctly says it models eyewitness events, but later sections repeatedly interpret outputs as population spread.
Spatial validation uses confirmed positives both to choose the origin and to judge the envelope.
Vancouver and another distant point are excluded after viewing the outcome, creating post-hoc validation bias.
The printed longitude `22.418612 W` is incompatible with the Washington/Vancouver map and is likely a missing leading digit; it must not be silently corrected.
Choosing the earliest point in the central cluster as the propagation origin has no origin-sensitivity analysis.
"Basically includes" in Figure 4-2 is not quantified by coverage, false-area ratio or a held-out metric.
The number of `d_max` simulations, random seed, parameters and fitted-distribution diagnostics are absent.
A mean simulated distance below a cited maximum does not demonstrate model accuracy.
Equation 4-7 is an ad hoc confidence map with no probability calibration.
Equation 4-7 defines distance `d` but uses `x` in its second branch.
Table 4-1 displays only thirteen cases per class; the relationship to all labeled records is not explained.
The `84.6%` sentence attaches the number ambiguously even though it comes from two negative false positives.
The spatial model has no sealed train/test or temporal holdout.
LDA's bag-of-words independence loses word order, negation and phrases important to sighting descriptions.
LDA classification confidence is semantically unclear: some rows classified positive have values near 0.07-0.09, while "unknown" is exactly 0.5.
The unknown threshold and whether confidence means positive probability, error probability or distance are not defined.
Table 5-2 shows thirteen examples per class, while the complete text-corpus counts and missing Notes are not reconciled.
Figure 5-2 does not clearly declare normalization axes or raw confusion counts.
The explanation that few positive texts cause below-50% accuracy is plausible but not isolated with resampling or learning curves.
Tokens such as `WSDA` can leak workflow/source identity instead of insect morphology.
The external Kaggle bee-versus-wasp corpus has different labels, acquisition conditions and class composition from agency reports.
External and supplied images can have severe domain shift, but no source-stratified performance table is reported.
The TRAIN/VALIDATION/TEST membership, random seed, stratification and duplicate grouping are not frozen.
Saying random data are selected from train, validation and test risks using the held-out set during model development.
A six-layer CNN description plus 32x32 input is insufficient to reproduce filters, pooling, optimizer, learning rate, batch size or augmentation.
Resizing small insect details to 32x32 can erase diagnostic morphology.
The highest 91.75% across epochs is reported without a preregistered checkpoint or final test value.
The CNN evaluation paragraph mistakenly calls the image model a text-identification model.
Equation 5-14 never defines how `w1,w2,w3` are computed from effective information or normalized.
Spatial, LDA and CNN outputs are combined as probabilities without evidence that they share calibration or meaning.
Table 5-3 likely corresponds to 13/14 positives and about 2,722/3,194 negatives, but does not state those counts.
The verified labels appear to be used throughout construction, weighting and evaluation, so independence is unproven.
Lower fused point confidences are called more reliable merely because class fit exceeds 80%; no calibration comparison supports this.
For the two anomalies, text and image scores are high even though the prose says longer text and unclear images reduce their credibility.
The two final anomaly scores near 0.54 cannot be reproduced from the displayed component values without the missing weights.
S-E thresholds are equal-width conventions rather than cost-, capacity- or risk-calibrated decision boundaries.
Letting staff abandon E-level reports is unsafe without target recall, false-negative cost, quarantine and appeal analysis.
The forgetting update treats negative reports as hardly affecting prediction without empirical support and adds one `D_neg` quantity to both text and image corpora.

The 75-day no-positive rule cannot prove eradication under imperfect detection; the circular `R_now`, repeated metric conflict, same-data before/after test and memorandum's abandonment advice all require independent operational validation.
